ai.title: Adjust main-prompt instructions to prevent infinite loops
ai.summary: Commented out the standalone system instruction block in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` after it failed to prevent infinite loops. Updated the `previous_assistant_message` correction prompt to trigger only when `prompt && hasAssistantMessage` is true, changing its `timeToLive` from `agentStep` to `userPrompt`. This restricts the instruction to per-user-prompt execution, preventing it from persisting indefinitely across agent steps.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question, it now checks the previous response for mistakes only once per question, instead of repeating that check on every internal step, which had caused it to get stuck looping. You won't see any visible change in how the assistant behaves, but it will no longer freeze or repeat itself when working through a question.

ai.title: Add /export command for conversation summaries
ai.summary: Added /export slash command to CLI and backend prompts, generating Markdown summaries of conversation decisions, file changes, and reasoning. Implemented in backend/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts, npm-app/src/cli.ts, and npm-app/src/menu.ts. Saves files prefixed with codebuff-export- in project root.

eli5.text: When you are planning something with the assistant, you can now type "export" as a command to make it write a neatly formatted summary of your whole conversation, like the decisions you made, any files discussed, and the reasoning behind them, into a text file saved in your project folder, prefixed with "codebuff-export-. This works right away when you use the command, and the assistant creates the file for you using its writing tool. If you are using the planning mode, you'll also see a tip suggesting this export option after you switch into that mode.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.305
ai.summary: npm-app/package.json version updated from 1.0.304 to 1.0.305. Internal release increment. No functional code changes.

eli5.text: If you've been using the assistant, updating to this version lets you type a new /export command that turns your current conversation into a clean Markdown summary, showing the decisions made, files changed, and reasoning, which you can save or share. Behind the scenes, this release also bundles several smaller refinements: the assistant now closes its connection cleanly when the program exits, stops repeating itself in prompts thanks to new anti-loop instructions, and can tap into a couple of newly tuned models for picking up files faster. The version number itself just ticks up by one as part of a routine packaging step, but the real difference you'd notice is that export option now showing up in your menu of commands.

ai.title: Reorganize agent messages for prompt caching
ai.summary: Reordered and restructured message array in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. User prompt and relevant context moved earlier to stabilize prefix for prompt caching. Removed dead code and debug logging for tool results.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the system has reordered the instructions it prepares before responding to you so that your recent question and any relevant context sit at the very start of the instruction bundle. This reorganization is an optimization that makes the system faster and more consistent when it relies on a cached prefix of its own instructions, and it also removes a couple of old, unused helper steps and a debugging log that nobody needed anymore. The net effect to you is invisible: responses come back the same, just a little bit more efficiently when the system can reuse its pre-computed instruction prefix.

ai.title: /compact command replaces message history with summary
ai.summary: Added `/compact` command to summarize and replace conversation history. Backend `main-prompt.ts` swaps `messageHistory` with a single user message containing the summary when detected. CLI `npm-app/src/cli.ts` and `menu.ts` handle input forwarding and UI registration. `system-prompt/prompts.ts` defines the summarization instructions.

eli5.text: You can now type /compact during a conversation to have the assistant condense everything discussed so far into a brief summary, replacing the full transcript going forward. After running it, the chat continues from that summary instead of carrying the entire back-and-forth history. This is live today for anyone interacting with the assistant.

ai.title: Add --ask CLI flag for question-only mode
ai.summary: Introduces the `--ask` command-line option to Freebuff, enabling a 'questions & planning only' mode that prevents code changes. The flag maps to `costMode = 'ask'` in `npm-app/src/index.ts` and is registered in `npm-app/src/cli-definitions.ts`. Convenience scripts `start-ask` are added to both root and `npm-app` `package.json` files.

eli5.text: The assistant can now enter a question-only mode where it discusses and plans work but will not directly edit your code. If you launch it with the new option, you will see the same assistant behavior, just with code changes turned off, letting you review and guide the plan before anything touches your files. This is a minor, internal addition, so it takes effect immediately whenever someone enables the new flag.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.306
ai.summary: Bumped package version from 1.0.305 to 1.0.306. Applied to `npm-app/package.json`. No functional changes.

eli5.text: If you installed this release it now reports a newer build number, but you won't see any difference because nothing inside actually changed. The other items listed alongside it, like a new command to summarize long conversations and a question-only mode, are already live and ready to use today.

ai.title: Fix main-prompt test
ai.summary: Updated backend/src/__tests__/main-prompt.test.ts to use dynamic index lookups for message history assertions instead of hardcoded positions. Removed brittle checks for intermediate instruction messages and strict cache control assertions. Scope limited to test file; no production code changes. Minimum message history length expectation reduced from 4 to 3 to match actual flow.

eli5.text: The software's self-check that verifies it remembers the right conversation pieces now looks for messages by what they say instead of assuming they sit in fixed spots, so the check no longer fails when the order shifts. A behind-the-scenes quality check used by builders was corrected; if you use the app you won't see anything different, but the system is slightly less likely to mistake a memory slip for a real bug.

ai.title: Reorder interactive command menu to non-alphabetical priority
ai.summary: Removed alphabetical sort from getSlashCommands in npm-app/src/menu.ts. Commands now display in explicit array order, prioritizing init before login and grouping compact, export, and ask near reset. Description for reset updated to 'conversation history'. Scope limited to CLI interactive menu.

eli5.text: When you open the interactive command menu in Codebuff, the list of slash commands now appears in a hand-picked order instead of alphabetized. The most important commands like starting a project (init) and logging in come first, while housekeeping commands like clearing history and saving summaries sit near the end with the exit option. You also won't see the word 'context' in the reset command description anymore, it now just says it clears your conversation history. This menu only affects people using the interactive CLI mode, not anyone running commands directly.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.307
ai.summary: Version in npm-app/package.json bumped from 1.0.306 to 1.0.307. Scope limited to package.json. No functional changes.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant, it can now follow your instructions without getting stuck in endless loops, and a new /export command lets you save a summary of your conversation. The command menu also now shows its options in a priority-based order instead of alphabetical, so the most useful commands appear near the top. These fixes and additions are available to everyone using the assistant as of June 1, 2025.
